experiment_description: Device-independent two-point-measurement certification of a local qubit quantum memory is implemented on a trapped-ion processor to test whether temporal correlations can rule out a classical, entanglement-breaking memory model without trusting device internals. The processor consists of a linear chain of three ground-state-cooled 40Ca+ ions in a macroscopic linear Paul trap; the two outer ions encode qubits A′ and E, while the middle ion is a spacer to reduce optical addressing cross-talk over the ion-chain length. Qubit manipulation uses an individually addressed 729 nm laser with linewidth below 1 Hz incident at 67.5 degrees to the trap axis through a crossed-AOD addressing system; state readout uses resonant 397 nm fluorescence collected on an EMCCD camera, with fluorescence corresponding to population in the S1/2 manifold and absence of fluorescence to population in the D5/2 manifold. The sequence prepares the two outer ions A′+E in a Bell state using a Mølmer-Sørensen entangling gate. Qubit E is spectroscopically shelved into unused D5/2 levels during the mid-circuit measurement on A′ to reduce measurement back-action. The first measurement setting X is sampled from four Pauli choices {σx, σz, −σx, −σz}, with binary outcome A. A measure-and-prepare instrument is implemented so that the post-measurement qubit A is prepared in a σx eigenstate depending only on A and not on X; in the memory-test assignment, outcome A=1 corresponds to |+⟩ and A=0 corresponds to |−⟩, with equivalent sign conventions handled by post-processing of the four X settings. After readout, Doppler and polarization-gradient recooling are applied because the fluorescence measurement heats the shared motional mode; resolved sideband recooling is not used after the mid-circuit measurement in order not to disturb E. With no deliberately added storage-delay sweep in this certification run, qubits A+E undergo a CNOT gate followed by a virtual full SWAP, where the CNOT is composed of one Mølmer-Sørensen interaction and local rotations R^C_0(π/2), R^T_π(π/2), R^T_{π/4}(π), MS^C,T_XX(π/2), and R^T_{π/2}(π/2). The second-time qubit B is measured in the (σx+σz)/√2 basis. Repeated runs over the four X settings produce the empirical probabilities Pr(A,B|X). The device-independent memory witness is Γ = Σ_{b0,b1} inf_{x∈{0,1,2,3}} Σ_{a∈{0,1}} Pr(A=a,B=b_a|X=x), whose classical instrumental bound is Γ≥1. The reported qubit-memory quality is the Uhlmann fidelity FMemory between the Choi-Jamiołkowski state of the implemented memory channel and that of an ideal identity memory, lower-bounded from Γ using FMemory ≥ 1/2[1 − (Γ − 2 + S_K)/(√2 − S_K)], with S_K=(8+7√2)/17. To assess cross-talk in the same spatially local ion-chain geometry, the Pearl parameter Δ = max_a Σ_b sup_x Pr(A=a,B=b|X=x) is computed, and the average causal direct effect is defined as ACDE = sup |Pr(B_do(A=a,X=x)=b) − Pr(B_do(A=a,X=x′)=b)| over the indicated binary outcomes and settings; in this implementation the same empirical probability table and post-processed intervention assignments are used to estimate these quantities.

instrumental_inequality_gamma.description: The measured value of the device-independent two-point-measurement memory witness Γ computed from Pr(A,B|X).

memory_fidelity_lower_bound_fraction.description: The device-independent lower bound on the fidelity of the implemented qubit memory channel to an ideal identity memory channel.

classical_memory_model_excluded.description: Whether the measured temporal correlations exclude the classical instrumental-memory bound for the tested qubit memory configuration.

pearl_cross_talk_parameter_delta.description: The measured Pearl-inequality parameter Δ used as an observational witness for possible cross-talk influences from X to B not mediated by A.

average_causal_direct_effect.description: The measured average causal direct effect quantifying direct cross-talk influence from the first measurement setting X to the later outcome B under interventions fixing A.

experiment_description: Temporal classicalisation of the same device-independent two-point-measurement qubit-memory protocol is characterized by sweeping a storage waiting time between the mid-circuit measurement-and-repreparation step and the CNOT-plus-virtual-SWAP readout operation. The physical platform, spatial geometry, optical addressing, shelving of the E ion, 397 nm EMCCD fluorescence readout, recooling after the first measurement, first measurement settings X∈{σx, σz, −σx, −σz}, σx-eigenstate post-measurement preparation of qubit A, and final B measurement in the (σx+σz)/√2 basis are the same as in the no-delay certification sequence. The added waiting time is swept from 0 ms to 100 ms. During this interval, dynamical decoupling echo pulses are inserted every 2.5 ms to suppress quasi-static and 100 Hz magnetic-field noise, while active magnetic-field compensation suppresses the 50 Hz mains component. For every waiting time, repeated experimental shots over all four X settings provide Pr(A,B|X), from which the rescaled violation of the classicality inequality is computed; positive rescaled values correspond to a violation of the classical temporal-causal bound, and the certification duration is determined from the waiting-time range over which the data still certify a non-classical qubit memory under the stated protocol.

certified_quantum_memory_duration_ms.description: The storage duration for which the two-point-measurement protocol certifies the trapped-ion qubit memory as non-classical.

experiment_description: A two-point-measurement experiment is performed on the same three-ion 40Ca+ trapped-ion processor to test non-classical causal relations by coherently varying the balance between common-cause and direct-cause mechanisms. The two outer ions encode A′ and E and the middle ion is a spacer; qubit control uses the 729 nm addressed laser at 67.5 degrees, and readout uses 397 nm fluorescence imaging on an EMCCD. The outer ions are initially prepared in a Bell state by a Mølmer-Sørensen gate. The first measurement on A′ uses the same four sampled Pauli settings X∈{σx, σz, −σx, −σz} with binary outcome A, while E is shelved during the mid-circuit measurement and the ion chain is recooled afterward. In this causal-relation protocol, the measure-and-prepare state of A is a σy eigenstate depending only on A: |+i⟩ for A=0 and |−i⟩ for A=1, with sign conventions handled by the four-setting post-processing table. The two-qubit operation after the first measurement is the partial-swap gate U_PS(α)=cos(α/2) id + i sin(α/2) U_swap, implemented as MS_ZZ(−α/2)·MS_YY(−α/2)·MS_XX(−α/2), where the rotation angle is controlled by laser intensity while keeping the gate time fixed. The independent control parameter α is swept over the interval 0 to π radians. The final measurement of B is σx. For each α, repeated runs over all X settings yield Pr(A,B|X), from which the same classical causal inequality witness is evaluated to determine whether the observed process can be simulated as a classical mixture of common-cause and direct-cause processes.

nonclassical_causal_relations_certified.description: Whether the partial-swap two-point-measurement data certify causal relations outside classical common-cause/direct-cause mixtures for some swept gate angles.

alpha_interval_with_reported_classical_i.description: The reported swept partial-swap angle interval in which the measured causal witness violates the classical causal bound.

experiment_description: The effective coherence time relevant to the trapped-ion quantum-memory decay model is characterized independently with Ramsey-type measurements on the same 40Ca+ trapped-ion processor. The qubit is manipulated with the addressed 729 nm laser and read out by 397 nm fluorescence imaging, while the magnetic environment is treated as in the memory-decay experiment: active compensation suppresses coherent 50 Hz mains magnetic-field noise, and a dynamical-decoupling echo sequence with pulses separated by 2.5 ms suppresses quasi-static and 100 Hz components. Ramsey experiments are run over a waiting-time sweep spanning 0 ms to 200 ms, and the Ramsey contrast is fit with an exponential decay model corresponding to Lorentzian-distributed frequency noise. The fitted decay constant is used as the effective T2 coherence time of the trapped-ion qubit under the dynamical-decoupling conditions used for the quantum-memory certification sequence.

effective_coherence_time_T2_ms.description: The exponential Ramsey-contrast decay time of the trapped-ion qubit under the dynamical-decoupling conditions used in the memory experiment.
